items.excerpt: As AI systems become embedded across physics research — from particle detection to materials discovery — Physics World examines the 'black box' problem: researchers increasingly struggle to understand how these models reach their conclusions, raising questions about whether science is entering an era of discoveries without full comprehension.

items.excerpt: Researchers at the University of Osaka trained an AI model on molecular-dynamics simulations to evaluate 16 structural descriptors and identify the most effective ways to distinguish water's two competing liquid states, helping pin down a hidden 'critical point' in supercooled water and clarifying the origin of water's anomalous properties.

items.excerpt: Brown University researchers show that physics-informed neural networks combining Fick's law of diffusion with sparse experimental data can accurately predict long-term drug-release rates from controlled-release patches and bandages, matching outcomes using roughly 6% of the data for simple geometries and about 33% for complex ones.

items.excerpt: Scientists at the GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences used artificial intelligence to detect previously hidden slow-slip ('silent') events on California's San Andreas Fault, finding these creeping fault movements are followed by measurably increased seismic activity — a new AI-enabled window into earthquake precursors.
items.note: NEW. On-list (phys.org). Verified via WebFetch: published July 9, 2026; freshness.py science -> FRESH. AI applied to geophysics/seismology discovery. phys.org item 2 of 3. Not in exclusion list.

items.excerpt: North Carolina State University researchers built BINND (Binding and Interaction Neural Network for DNA), a deep-learning model trained on 144 million DNA sequence pairs that predicts which DNA strands bind to one another with 83.5% accuracy — at least 10% better than prior methods — with applications in DNA computing, data storage and diagnostics.

items.excerpt: GEN surveys how AI-based 'virtual cell' foundation models are moving multiscale — integrating molecular, cellular and tissue-level data to predict how cells respond to genetic and chemical perturbations — reshaping drug discovery through better therapeutic targeting and disease modeling.

items.excerpt: Quanta explores thermodynamic computers — chips (from startups Normal Computing and Extropic) that harness thermal fluctuations and noise to compute, promising to run generative-AI algorithms with dramatically lower energy use, a physics-driven rethink of the hardware substrate underlying modern AI.

items.excerpt: MIT CSAIL researchers built 'SceneSmith,' a system that uses three collaborating AI agents to assemble realistic 3D indoor scenes — objects, walls and overall look — giving robots virtual playgrounds to practice skills and generate the training data they need before real-world deployment.
